text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Ulcerative Colitis. Given the classic presentation of bloody diarrhea, urgency, mucus, and relief with defecation, along with the recent exposure to a sick contact suggesting a potential infectious trigger, this clinical picture strongly points to Inflammatory Bowel Disease. While Campylobacter is a consideration, the chronic four-month duration and specific symptom profile make Ulcerative Colitis the primary diagnosis.
